observation.visible_scene: A white tabletop. A triangular frame built from segmented silver magnetic bars, with a large polished steel sphere resting at the top apex and an inner bar running from the apex toward the base, sits on the table. A pair of hands interacts with it, then a separate cluster of small shiny steel spheres is handled on the left side of the frame.
visible_changes: Frames 1-11 (continuous): both hands hold and fine-tune the magnetic-bar triangle. In frame 1 the hands grip the two slanted upper bars near the apex; from frame 2 onward the hands shift to the bottom-left and bottom-right vertices and keep them pinched, with only small positional adjustments. The triangle and its top sphere remain in roughly the same place in the frame throughout this interval (camera static).

Between frame 11 and frame 12 there is an editing cut: the framing/angle changes abruptly so the triangle moves to the right side of the frame and a grey-sleeved left arm enters from the bottom-left. This is a discontinuity, not smooth camera motion.
Frames 12-15 (after the cut): the left hand reaches to the far-left edge and draws a small cluster of shiny spheres into view; the triangle on the right stays untouched and stationary.

Frames 16-41 (continuous): both hands hold and knead/reshape the cluster of small steel spheres on the left; the cluster's outline and the visible arrangement of balls change as the hands turn and press it, while the triangle structure on the right remains fixed and unmodified.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the magnetic-bar triangle was assembled before frame 1, and whether the hands were tightening, aligning, or merely stabilizing it.
What the small-sphere cluster is being made into, and whether it will ever contact the triangle (it stays separate within this excerpt).
The reason for the cut between the two views and what occurred during the omitted time.
uncertain_details: Exact material of the bars and spheres (only appearance as metallic/magnetic is supported).
Whether the slight shifts of the triangle in frames 1-11 are hand-driven repositioning or just camera/hand jitter.
Precise frame boundary of the editing cut (it falls between samples 11 and 12).
